title: Enrich PagerDuty alerts with latency percentile snapshots and trace excerpts
creator: Ethan Cole
body: Goal: When an SLO/lambda alert fires and creates a PagerDuty incident, attach a compact snapshot showing 50/95/99 latency percentiles for the affected service and a 3-5 span trace excerpt (top error span + predecessor) to accelerate Triage and reduce time-to-resolution. Deliverables: 1) PD enrichment lambda that consumes observability events, composes attachments (JSON with percentiles + trace excerpt summary), and calls the PagerDuty Events V2 API; 2) Safe fallback that uploads large artifacts to signed S3 URLs and includes a short link in the PD incident; 3) Option to include a linkable runbook section and a link to the related dashboard time window; 4) Integration tests and rollout via feature flag with canary orgs. Engineering notes and tradeoffs: - Payload size: PagerDuty Events V2 supports limited payload sizes for triggered incidents. We cap inline attachments at 32KB; larger artifacts are uploaded to S3 and linked. - Trace excerpts are trimmed using the runtime summarizer: extract top-error span + up to two ancestors, limit to 8KB of serialized text (spans + tags). This preserves context without leaking full traces. - Security: Signed S3 URLs expire in 1 hour; links include a short nonce and HMAC to prevent tampering. KMS-managed key usage for any persisted metadata. - Routing: The enrichment lambda runs in the observability account and signs the payload with the observability service identity; PagerDuty routing rules unchanged. - Backpressure: If enrichment service is behind load, incidents should still be created with a minimal payload containing service/name/alert-id and a note "enrichment delayed"; enrichment worker will attach an addendum when ready. - Failure modes: If the enrichment attach call fails repeatedly, escalate to ops channel and add a short link to a cached dashboard so responders have a starting point. - Privacy: We scrub PII and customer identifiers from spans per the PII redaction policy before any external link is created. Implementation plan: 1) Schema design for PD attachment JSON and S3 artifact format (open doc in confluence). 2) Lambda/service to assemble attachments: fetch metrics snapshot from metrics-store, fetch trace from trace-store by trace_id, summarize, redact, encrypt if needed, and attach. 3) PagerDuty client library wrappers and retries with exponential backoff. 4) Slack/Consolidated channel integration: when PD incident is created, also post a short thread to the related Slack channel with the same snapshot and link. 5) Tests: unit, integration against PD staging account, and chaos injection that simulates large traces and network failures. 6) Canary rollout and monitoring of any increase in PD API errors or enrichment latency. Metrics to observe: PD API success rate, enrichment attach latency (p95/p99), percentage of incidents with enrichment attached, number of fallback S3 links created, error rate on redact/summarizer. Rollout: Feature-flagged by org. 0% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 24-hour observation windows between steps. Fall-back plan: Toggle feature flag off to stop attachments without impacting incident creation. Postmortem automation: When an incident is resolved, if the attachment included a trace excerpt and the incident severity >= P1, auto-create a skeleton postmortem in the postmortem repo with links to the PD incident, S3 artifact, and dashboard snapshot (opt-in via org setting).
comments: 2025-03-06 - Priya: scoped initial schema; leaning toward 32KB inline cap to balance PD limits and UX. Added S3 fallback. Blockers: confirm PD staging quota and S3 signing policy.
2025-03-09 - Security review kickoff (Nadia): flagged redaction and S3 link expiry requirements, asked for KMS usage for any persisted attachments. Priya to update design.

2025-03-12 - Engineering sync: decided to reuse the existing trace summarizer lib (trace-summarizer v0.9) and extend to annotate anchor spans with service topology. Added dependency on ENG-31782 for runbook attachment hooks.
2025-03-15 - QA: wrote integration tests against PagerDuty staging; discovered intermittent 429s from PD. Added jittered retry logic and circuit-breaker for high 429 rates.
2025-03-18 - Devops: ready to deploy enrichment lambda to observability-staging; will enable flag for Redwood-internal orgs only. Noted to monitor PD API quotas during canary.
2025-03-18 - PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/842 is open, requesting review from @leo and @nadia.
acceptance_criteria: PagerDuty incidents created by the alerting pipeline include a latency snapshot and trace excerpt for >90% of test incidents in staging
If attachment size >32KB the service uploads artifact to signed S3 URL and the PD incident contains a secure short link
All attachments pass the PII redaction check in the security pipeline
Enrichment failures do not prevent incident creation; a clear note is present in the incident when enrichment is delayed
Automated tests (unit + integration) are included and passing in CI; PD staging integration test is green
Feature flag controls (org-level) are implemented and documented; canary rollout executed without increase in incident handling time or PD quota exhaustion
implementation_steps: Define PD attachment JSON schema and S3 artifact format and publish design doc
Implement enrichment service: metrics snapshot fetcher, trace summarizer integration, PII scrubber
Implement PagerDuty client wrapper with retries, backoff, and circuit-breaker
Add Slack posting hook for incidents with attachments; respect channel rate limits
Add unit and integration tests; configure PD staging creds in CI
Run canary rollout for internal orgs, monitor PD API usage and enrichment latency
Iterate on redact heuristics based on Security feedback and QA findings
Enable postmortem skeleton creation for P1 incidents as opt-in setting per org
